summary: Streaming chat disconnects / stalls mid-generation (SSE/WebSocket) causing partial responses
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Health, enterprise) reports streaming chat responses over SSE and WebSocket disconnecting or stalling mid-generation. Users receive partial output, or the stream silently closes after ~15-40s. Impact: production traffic for Acme Health; patient-facing chatflows truncated leading to support escalations.

Impact:
- Intermittent truncated responses for interactive chat.
- Increased user retries and support tickets.
- Observed across multiple models (gpt-rlhf-3b, gpt-rlhf-7b) and only in us-east region.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (customer routed to dedicated cluster via routing policy).
- SDK: open-source redwood-js v1.12.0 using WebSocket streaming.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Open WebSocket connection to streaming endpoint with continuation-enabled chat session.
2) Send a prompt that generates ~300-600 tokens (longer generation).
3) Observe streaming for initial tokens; then stream stalls or connection drops after 15-40s.
4) Retry sometimes returns full response; other times stalls replicate.

Logs / error excerpts:
- Client sees: "websocket: close 1006 - unexpected EOF" and occasional "upstream closed" messages.
- Proxy logs (excerpt): "streaming proxy: connection reset by peer after 22.4s; upstream last-write 22.1s".
- Serving runtime: some worker threads showing "tokenization paused" timeouts; no 5xx spike visible in public API metrics.

Notes: Customer reported first occurrence 2026-02-19 PDT; spike in reports on 2026-02-20. Ticket opened by CS on 2026-02-20.
steps_to_reproduce: Open WebSocket/SSE connection to /v1/streams with customer API key and start a chat session
Send a long prompt that expects 300-600 tokens of output
Observe streaming tokens for 15-40s then connection stalls or closes with code 1006
Repeat across gpt-rlhf-3b and gpt-rlhf-7b to confirm reproduction
logs:
[streaming-proxy] 2026-02-20T02:14:12Z WARN connection reset by peer id=abcd-1234 duration=22.4s upstream_last_write=22.1s
[serving-runtime] 2026-02-20T02:14:12Z DEBUG kv-cache miss seq=256 worker=13
[api-gateway] 2026-02-20T02:14:12Z ERROR websocket close 1006 client_ip=1.2.3.4 route=/v1/streams
Customer-client stacktrace: ERR_WS_CLOSED_BEFORE_COMPLETE
comments: 2026-02-20 Diego Martinez (SRE): Acknowledged. Assigned to SRE streaming team for immediate triage. Asked customer for SDK and server region; requested request IDs and sample timestamps.

2026-02-20 Customer (Acme Health): Provided two request IDs: req-20260220-7a1 and req-20260220-9f3. Using redwood-js v1.12.0 from browser clients. Reported ~20% of sessions affected during a 2-hour window.

2026-02-21 Priya Rao (Support Eng): Reproduced locally against prod-us-east using same SDK version and prompt set. Observed stream stall at approx 27s for one session; captured full proxy and runtime logs. Opening investigation with networking and runtime teams.

2026-02-21 Liam O'Connor (Networking): Noted a surge in RST packets between streaming-proxy and runtime cluster between 02:10-02:40Z. Correlated with short-lived kernel-level retries on a subset of frontend hosts. Investigating recent kernel update rollout.

2026-02-22 Diego Martinez (SRE): Rolled back streaming-proxy kernel patch on 3/5 affected frontends as a mitigation; customer reports immediate improvement in reduced disconnects. Continuing to monitor.
2026-02-23 Priya Rao (Support Eng): Confirmed with customer that occurrence rate dropped from ~20% to <1% after mitigation. Marking as resolved pending full root-cause analysis and permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: increased end-to-end latency leading to idle timeouts in streaming-proxy. Metrics did not show obvious per-route latency increase, but kernel-level retransmits spiked.

Captured pcap from two affected frontends: observed TCP RST originating from kernel TX path after ~22s of inactivity between proxy and runtime when connection held open and runtime continuously sending tokens.
Recent rollout: streaming-proxy hosts rolled kernel backports for improved socket buffer handling on 2026-02-18. Rollback on subset of hosts correlated with disappearance of RSTs.

Serving runtime: no evidence of OOM or worker crashes; token generation persisted in logs and runtime kept writing to socket until it received RST. Suggests network/kernel-level issue rather than runtime bug.

Related incidents: SUP-8421 and SUP-9123 reported similar symptoms in other customers—those tickets traced to transient proxy edge overloads rather than kernel bug. This incident appears distinct and linked to kernel backport rollout.
resolution:
Mitigation: Rolled back recent kernel backports on affected streaming-proxy hosts and rebalanced traffic away from affected frontends. Customer observed immediate drop in disconnects.
Permanent fix: Scheduled coordinated rollback across fleet and follow-up kernel vendor engagement for root-cause and re-release plan.
Postmortem: Create internal postmortem and update streaming-proxy runbook to include kernel rollout checklist and extra monitoring for TCP RST spikes.
resolution_notes: 2026-02-22 04:10Z - Partial rollback applied to 3/5 affected frontends; immediate customer improvement observed.
2026-02-22 10:40Z - Full rollback completed across us-east streaming-proxy fleet.
2026-02-23 09:00Z - Opened vendor support case with kernel vendor; collected pcap and system-logs and shared with vendor (case KERN-88123).
Follow-up actions: Add TCP RST alert to Redwood Console for streaming routes; add a preflight step to CI for kernel updates on streaming-proxy hosts; schedule postmortem by 2026-03-01.
